title: An Indian Immigrant's Son Just Entered One of America's Most Consequential Senate Races
excerpt: Dr Nirav Shah, who led Maine through COVID-19 and served as the CDC's second-in-command, is now running for Susan Collins's Senate seat. If he wins the nomination, he would be the first South Asian to run for Senate from New England.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Dr. Nirav Shah is running for Susan Collins's Senate seat in Maine.
  • Shah's candidacy could mark the first South Asian Senate nominee from New England.
  • He previously served as Maine's CDC director and oversaw a successful pandemic response.
  • Democrats need a net gain of four Senate seats to reclaim the majority in November.
  • Shah's campaign reflects growing political engagement among Indian Americans.
The last time Maine replaced a sitting U.S. senator, the Cold War was still on. Susan Collins has held the seat for nearly three decades, winning five consecutive elections in a state that prizes independence over ideology. No Democrat has come close to unseating her. That changed on Thursday, when Dr Nirav Shah — epidemiologist, lawyer, and the son of immigrants from India — formally announced his candidacy for the seat after the party's original nominee, Graham Platner, withdrew amid sexual assault allegations. ## From pandemic briefings to the ballot Shah is not a conventional political candidate. He built his public profile not through campaign rallies but through daily COVID-19 briefings that drew tens of thousands of viewers across Maine. As the state's CDC director from 2019, he oversaw a pandemic response that gave Maine one of the lowest death rates in the country — a record that drew national attention and, eventually, a call from Washington. President Biden appointed Shah as Principal Deputy Director of the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the agency's second-highest post. He returned to Maine last year to run for governor, finishing first in raw votes in the June 9 Democratic primary but losing under the state's ranked-choice system to former House Speaker Hannah Pingree. Now he is pivoting to a Senate bid that could define whether Democrats take control of the chamber in November's midterms. ![Nirav Shah — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/d5/Nirav_Shah_at_the_2.0_Trailer_Launch.jpg) > **""And now it's time to focus on the future." ## A crowded field with days to decide Shah is not alone."** "The past few days have been frustrating and downright maddening for all of us here," Shah said in a video announcing his candidacy. "And now it's time to focus on the future." ## A crowded field with days to decide Shah is not alone. At least five Democrats jumped into the race within hours of Platner's withdrawal, including Troy Jackson, a fifth-generation logger and former state Senate president who announced on Wednesday night with endorsements from 54 state and local officials. Dan Kleban, co-owner of Maine Beer Company, and Jordan Wood, a former congressional staffer, have also declared. The Maine Democratic Party must name a replacement by July 27 — the state's ballot deadline. The process will unfold at a hastily arranged nominating convention, though the party has not yet announced how the vote will work. Republicans are unbothered. "Susan Collins has defeated every DC-anointed candidate Chuck Schumer has sent her way," said Samantha Cantrell, a regional spokesperson for Senate Republicans' campaign arm. "She'll defeat whichever loser comes out of this process as well."

CDC's Second-in-Command Position
![Susan Collins — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/39/Senator_Susan_Collins%2C_2023_%28cropped%29.jpg) ## Why the diaspora is watching Shah's candidacy carries weight beyond Maine's borders. Endorsed by South Asians for America and the Indian American Impact Fund during his gubernatorial run, he has spoken openly about his identity as the child of Indian immigrants in a state that is 93 per cent white. "As the son of immigrants from India, I know firsthand the sacrifices families make to build a better future," Shah said in an earlier statement. "Here in Maine, and across our country, Donald Trump is targeting immigrants and dividing our country." If selected as the nominee and elected in November, Shah would become one of the few Indian Americans to serve in the U.S. Senate — joining a short list that currently includes no South Asian representation in the chamber. His platform centres on lowering healthcare costs, expanding Medicare, and challenging corporate consolidation. The stakes extend well beyond one seat. Democrats need a net gain of four Senate seats in November to reclaim the majority, and Maine — with its moderate electorate and history of ticket-splitting — is considered one of their most realistic targets. Collins, 73, is running on her record as a centrist dealmaker, but her approval ratings have slipped since her vote to confirm Justice Brett Kavanaugh in 2018.
Political Stakes for Democrats
›Need a net gain of 4 Senate seats to regain majority.
›Maine is a key target for Democrats.
›Shah's candidacy could influence Indian American political engagement.
For Indian Americans watching from across the country, Shah's bid is a test of whether the community's growing political engagement — from local school boards to state legislatures — can translate into power at the highest levels of American government. The convention is expected within days. The clock is already running.
